canonical_question: Is the '42-CrMo steel substrate' relevant to the corrosion performance of the coating, or does it only affect the mechanical integrity of the bond?

question_variants.question: Is the '42-CrMo steel substrate' relevant to the corrosion performance of the coating, or does it only affect the mechanical integrity of the bond?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The provided text confirms the coating was prepared on a 42-CrMo steel substrate but does not discuss whether this substrate affects the coating's corrosion performance versus just mechanical integrity.

answers.answer: The text notes the coating was prepared on 42-CrMo steel and that trends in microstructure, hardness, oxidation, and corrosion were analyzed, but it does not isolate the substrate's role in corrosion performance specifically.
answers.conditions: room and high-temperature, oxidizing and corrosive
answers.measurement_outcome: trends in coating microstructure, hardness, oxidation, and corrosion resistance analyzed
answers.boundary_limitation: No data provided on the specific impact of the 42-CrMo substrate on corrosion performance.
evidence_spans: Based on comprehensive consideration, W, V, Ta, Ti, and Cr elements are used to develop a new refractory high-entropy alloy with both hardness and high-temperature oxidation resistance.

In this study, WVTaTiCr x RHEAs coating was prepared on the 42-CrMo steel surface using laser cladding, and the trends in the coating microstructure, hardness, high-temperature oxidation resistance, and corrosion resistance were analyzed by varying the Cr content.

source_evidence_spans: prepared using laser cladding on the 42-CrMo steel surface
